slides: Let's continue with overlapping groups, and look at the two kinds of questions.

slides.say: On the exam, overlap questions come in two kinds.
In the first kind, a fact is missing, so we can't know the exact size of the overlap. We can only find a range, the smallest it can be and the biggest it can be.
at: We can only find a range

slides.say: In the second kind, we get every fact we need. Then we can find the exact number in each region.

slides: Let's see both kinds on one simple example, a pizza.

slides.say: We order a pizza cut into six slices. We put mushrooms on four slices. Here they are, shaded.
Now we put olives on three slices. Where can the olives go? Let's try it in two different ways.
On the first pizza, we put all the olives on slices with mushrooms. All three olive slices have mushrooms. So three slices have both.
Can more than three slices have both? No, because there are only three olive slices. So three is the most.
On the second pizza, someone doesn't like mushrooms. So first we put olives on the plain slices. There are two plain slices, so two olive slices are used.
One olive slice is left, and no plain slice is left. So it has to go on a slice with mushrooms. No matter what we do, at least one slice has both.
at: at least one slice has both

slides.say: And we can't put olives on the same slice twice. A slice either has olives, or it doesn't.
So the number of slices with both is at least one, and at most three. That's a range, the first kind of question.
at: at least one, and at most three

slides.say: Now the second kind. The same pizza, six slices, mushrooms on four and olives on three. But now there's one more fact. Exactly one slice has no topping at all.
at: Exactly one slice has no topping

slides.say: Let's see what that fact does. Two slices have no mushrooms. One of them is the slice with no topping. So the other one must get olives.
at: So the other one must get olives

slides.say: There are three olive slices, and one of them is on a plain slice. So the other two olive slices are on mushroom slices.
at: So the other two olive slices

slides.say: So exactly two slices have both. It's not a range this time, it's one number. One more fact turned a range into an exact answer. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next part.
at: So exactly two slices have both
